AgentCore harness — Security and access controls (harness-security.html)
FIRST FULL AUDIT 2026-09-28. Literal facts.

=== IAM PERMISSIONS MODEL (#harness-iam-permissions) ===
Harness APIs require permissions on BOTH the harness resource AND the underlying
AgentCore Runtime (and optional Memory) resource. Literal table:

| API | Required IAM actions |
| InvokeHarness                  | bedrock-agentcore:InvokeHarness, bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime |
| InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand      | bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand, bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime |
| InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell | bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell   <-- ONLY ONE ACTION |
| CreateHarness | CreateHarness, CreateAgentRuntime, CreateMemory |
| UpdateHarness | UpdateHarness, UpdateAgentRuntime, UpdateMemory |
| DeleteHarness | DeleteHarness, DeleteAgentRuntime, DeleteMemory |
| GetHarness | GetHarness |  ListHarnesses | ListHarnesses |
| CreateHarnessEndpoint | CreateHarnessEndpoint, CreateAgentRuntimeEndpoint |
| UpdateHarnessEndpoint | UpdateHarnessEndpoint, UpdateAgentRuntimeEndpoint |
| DeleteHarnessEndpoint | DeleteHarnessEndpoint, DeleteAgentRuntimeEndpoint |
| GetHarnessEndpoint | GetHarnessEndpoint | ListHarnessEndpoints | ListHarnessEndpoints |
| ListHarnessVersions | ListHarnessVersions |

*** ASYMMETRY: InvokeAgentRuntimeCommandShell is the ONLY invoke API that does NOT
    also require bedrock-agentcore:InvokeAgentRuntime. A principal explicitly denied
    InvokeAgentRuntime can still open a persistent interactive shell in the microVM. ***

ARN shapes:
  arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:<region>:<accountId>:harness/<id>
  arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:<region>:<accountId>:harness/<id>/harness-endpoint/<endpointName>
Get/Update/DeleteHarnessEndpoint require BOTH harness ARN and endpoint ARN.
CreateHarnessEndpoint requires only the harness ARN.
Invoking a custom endpoint: InvokeHarness and InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand require both ARNs.

=== MODEL CONFIGURATION PARAMETERS (#harness-model-params-security) ===
"The `model` field in InvokeHarness accepts additionalParams for Bedrock, OpenAI, and
LiteLLM configurations. These parameters are passed through to the underlying model
provider unchanged. The harness does not validate, filter, or restrict these parameters."
Callers who can set additionalParams can:
 * Redirect requests to arbitrary endpoints — LiteLLM `aws_bedrock_runtime_endpoint`
   overrides the Bedrock endpoint URL. "A caller can route the signed request -
   including the SigV4 signature and session credentials - to an endpoint that is
   specified in the trust model configuration."
 * Override HTTP headers — OpenAI `extra_headers` injects/overrides headers on the
   outbound request "including the Authorization header".
 * Attempt IAM role assumption — LiteLLM `aws_role_name` instructs the runtime to assume
   a different IAM role; succeeds/fails on the execution role's sts:AssumeRole perms.
 * Change the target model or region — `modelId` and `apiBase` can redirect inference to
   a different model, region, or provider entirely.
Suggested mitigations are CUSTOMER-side only (strip/allowlist the `model` field, remove
additionalParams/apiBase/modelId, deny sts:AssumeRole, VPC security groups).

=== SKILLS AND INSTRUCTIONS (#harness-skills-security) ===
Skills = markdown + scripts fetched from S3 or Git AT INVOCATION TIME and injected into
the agent's context. "The harness treats all skill content as trusted input. It does not
validate, sanitize, or inspect the content or source of skills."
*** "Skills can be overridden per InvokeHarness call." A caller can supply their own
    skill sources containing arbitrary instructions or scripts. ***
Customer responsibility: trust S3/Git sources, review markdown+embedded scripts, control
which principals can override the `skills` field.

=== TRUST BOUNDARY (#harness-trust-boundary) ===
"Any principal that passes the IAM or JWT authentication and authorization gate has access
to the full microVM session, including the tools and capabilities configured on the harness.
The harness validates the structure of the request it accepts, but it does not inspect the
meaning of prompts, screen content, or enforce behavioral constraints on the agent."
SERVER-SIDE PROTECTION THAT DOES EXIST: the harness REJECTS a `toolUse` block in the FINAL
message of InvokeHarness, so a caller cannot name a tool and have it dispatched directly.
"The harness does not evaluate which tool the block names" — applies to built-in server-side
tools and inline functions alike.
*** "For AgentCore Runtime deployments (non-harness), AgentCore Runtime provides NO
    server-side protection." Customer entrypoint must strip toolUse blocks itself. ***
`toolResult` in the final message IS accepted; model resumes reasoning over it. For inline
function tools the harness stores the model-generated toolUse + pending execution in the
session; only the matching toolResult on the same runtimeSessionId can resume it.

=== IDENTITY ===
*** SigV4 gap (verbatim note): "When callers authenticate with SigV4 (AWS IAM), the harness
    does not propagate per-user identity into downstream tool calls." Per-user credential
    scoping in AgentCore Identity Token Vault (user-scoped OAuth token storage, on-behalf-of
    token exchange) is ONLY available with Bearer JWT via the OAuth inbound path.
    "SigV4 support for per-user identity is planned for a future release." ***
Inbound OAuth: customJWTAuthorizer w/ discoveryUrl + allowedClients. JWT constraints
configurable: allowed audiences, allowed clients, allowed scopes, custom claims.
IdP discovery reachable over PrivateLink: --private-endpoint-vpc-id (+subnets+ip-type
+security-groups) OR --private-endpoint-lattice-arn (mutually exclusive). CUSTOM_JWT only.

=== OBSERVABILITY ===
"The harness automatically propagates correlation identifiers to downstream AgentCore
primitives (Gateway, Memory, Code Interpreter, Browser)... These identifiers are used for
observability only - they are never used for authorization or data access decisions."

=== EXECUTION ROLE ===
Trust policy principal: bedrock-agentcore.amazonaws.com.
Default sample execution role Sids: BedrockModelInvocation, EcrPublicTokenAccess,
StsForEcrPublicPull, XRayTracingAccess, CloudWatchLogsGroup, CloudWatchLogsDescribeGroups,
CloudWatchLogsStream, CloudWatchLogsPutResourcePolicy, CloudWatchMetricsPublish,
AgentCoreWorkloadIdentity (GetWorkloadAccessToken, GetWorkloadAccessTokenForJWT),
AgentCoreBrowserDefault (7 browser actions incl. ConnectBrowserAutomationStream,
ConnectBrowserLiveViewStream), AgentCoreCodeInterpreterDefault (5 actions),
AgentCoreMemory (CreateEvent, DeleteEvent, GetEvent, ListEvents, RetrieveMemoryRecords).
*** The AWS-published sample grants bedrock:InvokeModel on
    arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/* AND arn:aws:bedrock:<region>:<acct>:* —
    AWS's own note: "allows invocation of all foundation models across all regions and
    all Bedrock resources in your account." The AgentCore CLI creates this role
    AUTOMATICALLY when you scaffold a harness project. ***
Workload identity name pattern: workload-identity/harness_<agentName>-*
Default managed memory name pattern: memory/harness_<agentNameAbbrv>_*
VPC-mode managed image repo: ecr repository/harness-<region>, AWS-owned account (wildcarded).
Optional add-on policies: lifecycle hook targets (lambda:InvokeFunction / sns:Publish /
events:PutEvents), private ECR, VPC managed image pull, customer Memory, custom Browser,
custom Code Interpreter, Gateway (InvokeGateway), skill S3 (s3:GetObject+ListBucket),
API key credential provider (GetResourceApiKey + secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on
bedrock-agentcore-identity!default/apikey/<name>-*), OAuth2 credential provider
(GetResourceOauth2Token + secret bedrock-agentcore-identity!default/oauth2/<name>-*).

=== SHARED RESPONSIBILITY (customer side, verbatim list) ===
Agent code security and dependency management; IAM access controls and resource policies;
security of commands executed in runtime sessions; session-to-user mapping enforcement;
input validation and prompt injection prevention; model configuration validation
(additionalParams, apiBase, modelId); skill and instruction sources; container image
updates; network configuration.
